supersessionReason: Independent acceptance review found that v7 did not apply exact-byte failure journaling and deterministic-head ordering to not-modified confirmations, and did not centrally filter every persisted event-identity column.

notModifiedIntegrity.deterministicHeadRule: a not-modified confirmation may publish only when its retained pointer is also the deterministic newest eligible usable publication; a newer stranded publication keeps the source stale and records a manifest failure
notModifiedIntegrity.exactByteRule: the retained response and sidecar must be recovered and verified before a not-modified event can publish
notModifiedIntegrity.permanentFailureRule: missing or corrupt retained evidence appends one deterministic corrupt_object failure and alert, keeps the forensic pointer non-current, and permanently excludes that capture from later not-modified confirmation
notModifiedIntegrity.transientFailureRule: a transient read failure appends one deterministic storage_failure and alert, keeps the pointer stale, and remains retryable after exact bytes recover
notModifiedIntegrity.clockRule: a not-modified event may clear failure state only when its confirmation time is not older than the latest attempt
notModifiedIntegrity.recoveryRule: a later exact-byte verification of the named deterministic newer head may resolve the ordering failure without refetching or relabeling the immutable publication

eventIdentitySecretFiltering.rule: every event identity and persistence column is secret-scanned before any insert statement is prepared
eventIdentitySecretFiltering.failureRule: a rejected identity writes no event, alert, manifest, pointer, or object

effectiveContract: source-capture-contract.2026.1 plus v2, v3 except its superseded same-batch pointer clause, v4 except its superseded manifest-time verification clause, v5, v6, v7, and every clarification in this file
